title: New Orleans music as a unique blend
summary: Cahn says jazz could only come from New Orleans, blending French martial music, Congo Square, riverfront labor and street vendors.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Yes, I've had to influence quite a bit of New Orleans music, but New Orleans music is just a real go-around. It's influenced by many, many things and influences many, many things. It seems to be just, as it has been said, these things could only happen in New Orleans because of the music. No other place in the world has the mixture that comes up with this creation. What do you mean by creation? The creation of the New Orleans music. When our smaller, you might call them semi-pro groups play, they still have the New Orleans beat to it. That's something that's not found any other place in the world.
And definitely deals with the social origin, with origin of ancestry.

Yes, or the Indians or the jazz. I mean, jazz could only have really come out of New Orleans because we had the French martial music, which had its influence. We've had the Congo Square dances every Sunday, which had its influence. We had the laborers on the riverfront, on the cotton. We had the market men. And even the extinct creature, the chimney sweep, had his.

And all of this has blended together to create music that is only found in New Orleans and has been exported elsewhere. Yeah, of course. I mean, it's really a beautiful thing. Our music is heard all over the world and probably... Probably...
appreciated less than New Orleans and any other place in the world.
